1.
Present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners being legal heirs of deceased Satyaveer Singh.

Facts in brief are that on 19.12.2016 at about 6.00 p.m. deceased Satyaveer Singh along with Prempal Singh was coming to Village Kanhaira from Ahmadgarh on motorcycle being driven by Satyaveer Singh at a normal speed and on correct side of road.

When their motorcycle reached near village Mumrejpur, PS Ahmadgarh, District Bulandshahar, UP, in the meanwhile a Santro car bearing registration no.DL-3CAB-2744 being driven by respondent no.1 at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner while violating traffic rules came from opposite side and changing its driving lance and hit the motorcycle with a great force.
As a result of such impact, motorcycle fell down on the road and both Satyaveer Singh and Prempal Singh received grievous injuries.
Satyaveer Singh was taken to Babu Banarsi Dass Rajkiya Chikitsalay, Bulandshahar, UP where first aid was given to him and he was referred to High Medical Centre.

Thereafter he was taken to GTB Hospital,
Delhi and his MLC NO.1652/2016 was prepared.
During the course of treatment deceased died on 20.12.2016.
It is stated that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
It is stated that respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and it was insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
MACT No.355/2017 Page 2 2

. A joint WS was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 wherein it is stated that accident was occurred due to negligency on the part of deceased as he was coming from wrong side with very high speed and driving it in rash and negligent manner.
It is stated that at the time of accident respondent no.1 was having valid driving licence to drive the vehicle in question and it was insured with United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
It is contended that petitioners got involved the vehicle of respondent no.2 in the said accident with malafide intention to extort money and respondents are not liable to pay any compensation.

3. In the WS filed on behalf of respondent no.3, an objection has been taken that this Court has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the present claim petition as the alleged accident occurred in Uttar Pradesh and petitioners are also residing in Uttar Pradesh.
Further objection taken is that owner and insurer of motorcycle allegedly driven by deceased have not been made parties in the present claim petition.
On merits it is stated that vehicle no.DL-3C-AB-2744 was insured with respondent no.3 being insurance policy no.2220023116P106062812 valid from 09.08.2016 to 08.08.2017.

It is denied that accident has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
4.

DL-3CAB-2744 on 19.12.2016 at about 6 pm near Village Mamrejpur, PS Ahmadgarh,
Distt.
Bulandshahar UP in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extend and from whom?

Issue No.1 7.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

9. Petitioners have also examined PW2 Bahadur Singh who deposed that he is eye witness in this case and well conversant with the MACT No.355/2017 Page 4 facts and circumstances.

PW2 deposed that on 19.12.2016 at about 06.00 p.m. Satyaveer Singh along with Mulchand were coming to Village Kanhaira from Ahmadgarh on motorcycle which was being driven by Satyaveer Singh at a normal speed and on correct side of road.
PW2 further deposed that he along with Bhura were also going on the same direction by motorcycle and following them.

He deposed that when they reached near Village Mumrejpur, PS Ahmadgarh, District Bulandshahar, in the meanwhile a Santro Car bearing registration no.DL-3CAB-2744 being driven by its driver at very high speed, rashly and negligently, in a zig zag manner came from opposite side and changing its driving lane and hit motorcycle of Satyaveer Singh with a great force.

As a result of that motorcycle fell down on the road and Satyaveer Singh sustained grievous injuries and he was taken to Banarshi Dass Rajkiya Chikitsalay, Bulandshahar, UP where first aid was given to him and then he was referred to Higher Medical Centre.
Thereafter injured was taken to GTB Hospital, Delhi where he died during the course of treatment on 20.12.2016 at 12.05 p.m.

PW2 also deposed that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by driver of Santro car no.DL-3CAB-2744 and a case crime no.287/2016 u/s 279, 338, 304A, 427 IPC, PS Ahmadgarh was registered.
10.
PW2 was cross-examined on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2.
During cross-examination PW2 stated that accident has taken place at night i.e. in the evening at about 06.00 p.m.

PW2 stated that Urmila vs Krishan Pal on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80688193/
3 deceased was going 20 metre ahead from PW2.
The headlight of the car as well as of motorcycle were on at the time of accident and sun had already set by that time.
PW2 further stated that traffic was normal at the time of accident and some vehicles were plying on the road.
PW2 reached at the spot of MACT No.355/2017 Page 5 accident after 02 minutes and driver of car fled away from the spot when he reached there.
PW2 stated that deceased was his nephew and his father name was Mahender Singh.
He admitted that when Mahender Singh reported the matter to police, PW2 was not present there.
He further stated that he narrated the story of accident to the father of deceased on next day.
PW2 further stated that motorcycle of Satveer thrown away 02 metres from the spot of accident at his left side.
He also stated that Prempal Singh also sustained injury in the accident as he was pillion rider of the deceased.

11. During cross-examination on behalf of respondent no.3/ insurance company, PW2 stated that after the accident he made a call at 100 number and after 10 minutes police officials reached at the spot.
PW2 stated that police recorded his statement on the very same day at the spot of accident.
He stated that width of the road is 20 feet and space in the left side of motorcycle was 2 feet.
He admitted that it was a head on collision.
12. Though eye witness PW2 was cross-examined but respondents have failed to put any dent to his testimony.

PW2 remained consistent that on the day of incidence he was following the motorcycle of the deceased and saw the occurrence of accident in which offending vehicle bearing no.DL-3CAB-2744 came from the wrong side being driven with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the deceased due to which he fell on the road sustained grievous injuries and due to such injuries he later died during the course of treatment.

Even otherwise perusal of certified copy of criminal case record Ex.P-1 shows that respondent no.1/driver was charge sheeted by the police of UP in criminal case being FIR No.287/2016 of PS Ahmadgarh for causing accident while driving offending vehicle bearing no.DL-3CAB-2744.
Site plan Ex.P-3 of the place of accident shows that it was a head on collision between the MACT No.355/2017 Page 6 motorcycle of deceased and offending vehicle.
Mechanical inspection report Ex.P-4 of the offending vehicle is also on record which shows that bonnet and front bumper of the said vehicle were found to be damaged.

13. Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.DL-3CAB- 2744 being driven by respondent no.1.
Issue No.2 14.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Satyaveer Singh.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Decided on 31.10.2017,
MACT No.355/2017 Page 7 laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

Urmila vs Krishan Pal on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80688193/
5 MACT No.355/2017 Page 8 Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.

The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
16.
Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
17.
Petitioner no.1 Smt.Urmila (PW1) in her evidence has proved copy of driving licence of deceased Satyaveer Singh as Ex.PW1/1.
Perusal of DL of deceased Ex.PW1/1 shows that date of birth of deceased was 10.07.1995.

As per this document,
age of deceased on the date of his death MACT No.355/2017 Page 9 was 21 years 05 months.
This document in the opinion of this Tribunal are conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of death of deceased due to accident (20.12.2016) was 21 years 05 months.
Assessment of Income of deceased :
18. Petitioner (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased husband was working as a labour and was earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month.
PW1 deposed that her husband was leading a peaceful and comfortable life with petitioners and had he not died in the accident, his income would have become more than doubled.
During cross-examination PW1 stated that his deceased husband was doing labour work at his native village in U.P.

PW1 admitted that she has not placed any proof of Urmila vs Krishan Pal on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80688193/
6 income of her deceased husband.
19.
No documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioners to prove the work and income of the deceased.

In the absence of any evidence and material either oral or documentary, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as a utensil seller or that he used to earn Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month at the time of his death.

In the absence of any such material this Tribunal income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in the State of U.P. which at the time of accident was of Rs.7,214.12 per month.

Application of Multiplier:
20.
As held above, deceased was 21 years 05 months of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the MACT No.355/2017 Page 10 judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:
 MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs  M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5 Age group between 66 and above 21.
In view of the above, multiplier of 18 has to be applied against the age bracket of 21 to 25 years to determine the compensation.

Future Prospects:
22.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.

In case the Urmila vs Krishan Pal on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80688193/
7 deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.

of the established MACT No.355/2017 Page 11 income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component."
23.

Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 21 years 05 months years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
24. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:

respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company has submitted that petitioners are entitled to consolidated amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium and no separate consortium to each of the legal heirs of deceased is required to be given.
In support of his submissions, ld. counsel has relied upon judgment in case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Somwati (2020) 9 SCC 644.

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners however submitted that in that judgment Apex Court has laid down that compensation under the heading "loss of love and affection" is inclusive in loss of consortium.
28. Having gone through the submissions and judgment relied upon in case of Somwati (supra).

Hon'ble Apex Court in Somwati's case (supra) in para 36 after explaining Filial consortium given to a parent of MACT No.355/2017 Page 13 deceased, parental consortium given to a child and Spousal consortium given to spouse, observed that consortium is not limited to spousal consortium and it also includes parental consortium as well as filial consortium.

In para 37 of the judgment it was observed that the Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi's case has referred to amount of Rs.40,000/-
to the "loss of consortium" but Constitution Bench had not addressed the issue as to whether consortium of Rs.40,000/- is only payable as spousal consortium.
It was further observed that judgment of Pranay Sethi cannot be read to mean that it lays down the proposition that the consortium is payable only to the wife.

In para 38 of the said judgment Hon'ble Apex Court did not accept the submission of counsel for appellant (insurance) that the amount of consortium awarded to each of the claimants is not sustainable.

In para 42 of the same judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court while referring to judgment in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kumar (2021) 11 SCC 780 and Sangita Arya vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (2020) 5 SCC 327 observed that in those judgments it is laid down that both spousal and parental consortium are payable.

In view of the pronouncement of Hon'ble Apex Court in Somwati's case (supra), this Tribunal is of the view that spouse, children and parents of deceased are entitled to compensation under the head of loss of consortium and there is no bar in limiting the consortium to a sum of Rs.40,000/- as a whole, as submitted by ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company in this case.

Therefore,
a compensation of Rs.44,000/-, 16,500/- and Rs.16,500/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
8.
13. Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.DL-3CAB- 2744 being driven by respondent no.1.
Issue No.2 14.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.

4
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
No documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioners to prove the work and income of the deceased.
In the absence of any evidence and material either oral or documentary, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as a utensil seller or that he used to earn Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month at the time of his death.
In the absence of any such material this Tribunal income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in the State of U.P. which at the time of accident was of Rs.7,214.12 per month.
As held above, deceased was 21 years 05 months of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 21 years 05 months years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
24. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)
25.
In para 42 of the same judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court while referring to judgment in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kumar (2021) 11 SCC 780 and Sangita Arya vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (2020) 5 SCC 327 observed that in those judgments it is laid down that both spousal and parental consortium are payable.
29. In view of the pronouncement of Hon'ble Apex Court in Somwati's case (supra), this Tribunal is of the view that spouse, children and parents of deceased are entitled to compensation under the head of loss of consortium and there is no bar in limiting the consortium to a sum of Rs.40,000/- as a whole, as submitted by ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company in this case.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
In support of his submissions, ld. counsel has relied upon judgment in case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Somwati (2020) 9 SCC 644.
Counsel for the petitioners however submitted that in that judgment Apex Court has laid down that compensation under the heading "loss of love and affection" is inclusive in loss of consortium.
It was further observed that judgment of Pranay Sethi cannot be read to mean that it lays down the proposition that the consortium is payable only to the wife.
